data.bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read past end of input buffer, triggered by truncated UTF-8 in an IRIREF)
data.rationale: terminal_IRIREF parses an IRI with the OPTIONAL_UNICODE_STRING loop (READ_UNICODE_STRING macro, tracker-sparql-grammar.h:1604), which calls g_utf8_get_char() without a max-length argument. When the scan reaches a UTF-8 lead byte at the last byte of the peeked input window (end), g_utf8_get_char keeps reading continuation bytes past 'end'. Since GBufferedInputStream allocates exactly buffer_size bytes, when the window ends at the allocation boundary (input fills the 4096-byte buffer), this reads past the heap allocation. Verified empirically: input of 4200 bytes, '<' + 4094 'a' + 0xF0 lead byte at offset 4095, fed to /out/fuzz_rdf_turtle produces 'AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1' in g_utf8_get_char called from terminal_IRIREF (grammar.h:1683), via parse_terminal (tracker-deserializer-turtle.c:254) from tracker_deserializer_turtle_iterate_next:688 (STATE_SUBJECT IRIREF terminal), through tracker_sparql_cursor_next <- tracker_data_load_from_deserializer <- tracker_direct_batch_update <- LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput. The root cause is the unbounded UTF-8 decode in the grammar terminal macros (also used by PN_PREFIX); fixing terminal_IRIREF/READ_UNICODE_STRING to bound reads by 'end' eliminates the crash.
